title: The name of the Passover
english: Before we begin the word-by-word reading of the Passover, a little should be said about the name itself, taken on its own.

Most of the brothers — perhaps all of them — take the name of the Passover from the Savior's passion, as if the feast were called pascha from that. But among the Hebrews this feast is not properly called pascha. It is called phas. The three letters of phas, with the heavier breathing they use, make up the name of the feast. If you translate it, it is crossing.
translator_notes: Origen's hedge τάχα kept as 'perhaps'.
φας left as phas (Origen's transcription of the Hebrew consonants). διάβασις rendered 'crossing', not 'Passover', so the etymology stays visible.
Witte letter-fills inside intact words (ἀδ[ελ]φῶν) are not shown in the English; restored whole words stay in square brackets.

title: The name of the Passover
english: For on this feast the people come out of Egypt, and so it is called phas, that is, crossing. The name cannot be spoken in Hebrew through the Greek tongue. The Greeks cannot say phas with the heavier breathing the Hebrews use. So the name was made Greek. In the prophets it is said phasek. When it has been more fully made Greek, it has been named pascha (Ezekiel 45:21) (2 Chronicles 35:1).

added_allusions.reason: The prophets' form φασὲκ / phasek.
LXX φασεκ / phasek in the prophets-and-writings form Origen names.

translator_notes: φασὲκ kept as phasek (the half-Hellenized form Origen names before πάσχα).

title: The name of the Passover
english: And if one of our people, rather rashly, should meet with Hebrews and say that the Passover was named from the Savior's passion, they will laugh at him as one who does not know at all what the name means — if they translate the name of the Passover properly, as the perfect among the Hebrews do.
translator_notes: Witte's <όμενο> in σημαιν<όμενο>ν taken as 'signified'.
οἱ τέλειοι: 'the perfect' among the Hebrews, not 'rabbis'.

title: The name of the Passover
english: This is enough about the name itself, taken on its own — enough to teach us what the name phas means, and enough to build us up: not to throw ourselves rashly at what is said in Hebrew, trying it without first knowing the Hebrew sense. Now we shall examine the words themselves. The Passover means crossing.
translator_notes: ἐπιβάλλειν taken as applying ourselves to the Hebrew sayings, not as attacking persons — the lesson of 1.3 is lexical caution.

title: What the Passover means for Christians
english: Since the people of the Hebrews then come out of Egypt, the law for this feast is given them, reasonably, household by household: each takes a male sheep, perfect and unblemished, sacrifices it, and toward evening eats it roasted with fire, neither raw nor boiled in water — so that the destroyer of the firstborn of the Egyptians may not touch them, seeing the posts of their doors anointed with the blood (Exodus 12:3–8) (Exodus 12:22–23) (Exodus 12:29).

added_allusions.reason: Male, perfect, unblemished sheep; roast with fire, not raw, not boiled.
Blood on the doorposts; the destroyer does not touch them.
Destroyer of the Egyptian firstborn.

translator_notes: φλιὰς: doorposts/posts; 'posts of their doors' keeps the later lintel/post distinction.

title: What the Passover means for Christians
english: When this has been done, the people come out of Egypt, and the firstborn of the Egyptians perish. After the Hebrews have gone out, Pharaoh regrets it. He comes out pursuing them with the army and the chariots, and so is drowned in the Red Sea. Moses with the people passes through the sea (Exodus 12:29–33) (Exodus 14:5–9) (Exodus 14:23–29).

added_allusions.reason: Firstborn perish; the people go out.
Pharaoh regrets the exodus and pursues with chariots.
Egypt drowned in the Red Sea; Israel passes through.

translator_notes: ἀπόλυται kept as 'perish' (not 'are released').

title: What the Passover means for Christians
english: That even to this day the Passover still takes place, and the sheep is sacrificed, and the people come out from Egypt — the apostle also teaches us, saying: "For our Passover also has been sacrificed, Christ; so let us keep the feast not with old leaven nor with leaven of malice and wickedness, but with unleavened bread of sincerity and truth." (1 Corinthians 5:7–8)

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: our Passover sacrificed, Christ; feast with unleavened sincerity and truth.

translator_notes: Quotation follows the papyrus wording, including εἱλικρινείας.

title: What the Passover means for Christians
english: And if our Passover has been sacrificed, Jesus Christ, those who sacrifice Christ come out of Egypt and pass through the sea and will see Pharaoh drowned. But if some of them want to go back into Egypt, they will not enter the holy land (1 Corinthians 5:7) (Numbers 14:3–4) (Exodus 16:3) (Hebrews 3:11–19).

added_allusions.reason: If our Passover has been sacrificed, Christ.
Wanting to return to Egypt and so not entering the land.
The wish to go back into Egypt.
Those who turn back do not enter.

translator_notes: Witte insertions <οἱ> and <βούλονταί> taken into the English as <those> / <want>.
θύειν of Christians 'sacrificing' Christ is Origen's own (holy eaters), not the crucifixion by the lawless — see 1.40–1.41.

title: Exodus 12:1–2
english: So that the mind that lies in the events of the history may be shown more fully in speech, we shall come to the words themselves, according to the letter.
translator_notes: κατὰ λέξιν: according to the letter / word by word, as in 1.1.

title: Exodus 12:1–2
english: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying: This month is for you the beginning of months; it is first for you among the months of the year (Exodus 12:1–2).

added_allusions.reason: Lemma quoted.

translator_notes: Lemma; wording follows Witte's LXX-like text (μὴν, not Attic μείς in the running quote).

title: This month is the beginning of months
english: This month, God says to Moses and Aaron, is a beginning of months, and first among the months of the year for them, when they come out of Egypt. And as far as the history goes, this same month is first, and the Jews keep this feast every year on the fourteenth of the first month, household by household, sacrificing a sheep according to the law given them through Moses (Exodus 12:1–6).

added_allusions.reason: First month; fourteenth; sheep by houses.

translator_notes: Witte insertion <θύοντες> kept as <sacrificing>.

title: This month is the beginning of months
english: But since Christ came not to abolish the law or the prophets but to fulfill them, he showed us what the true Passover is, the true crossing from Egypt (Matthew 5:17).

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: not to abolish the law or the prophets but to fulfill.

translator_notes: Witte restorations of 'the true Passover' / 'crossing from Egypt' kept in brackets.

title: This month is the beginning of months
english: And for the one who crosses, that is then a beginning of months, when the month of the crossing from Egypt comes. So for him a beginning of another birth comes: a new way of life for the one who has left the darkness and is coming to the light. I speak of the sign given through water to those who have hoped in Christ, which has been named a washing of regeneration. For what else does regeneration mean but the beginning of another birth (Titus 3:5) (John 3:3–5) (Colossians 1:12–13) (1 Peter 2:9)?

added_allusions.reason: Quoted sense: washing of regeneration.
Birth from above / water; another beginning.
From darkness to light.
Out of darkness into light.

translator_notes: πολιτεία: 'way of life', not 'citizenship' here (baptismal new life).

title: For you
english: A person must come inside a perfect way of life and perfect love, so that someone still in the present world may be able to hear: This month is the beginning of months for you (Exodus 12:2) (1 John 4:18).

added_allusions.reason: This month is the beginning of months — now with σοί, 'for you'.
Perfect love; possible frame for τελείας ἀγάπης.

translator_notes: σοί (singular) in this hearing-formula: the word is for the perfect, not the crowd.

title: For you
english: For this is not said by God to all the people, but only to Moses and Aaron. It is not written: "And God said to the people: This month is for you the beginning of months; it is first for you among the months of the year." (Exodus 12:1–3) It is written: "And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying: This month is for you the beginning of months; it is first for you among the months of the year." Then he adds: "Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth of this month let each take a sheep."

added_allusions.reason: Address to Moses and Aaron, then the tenth-day command to the congregation.

translator_notes: The counterfactual 'And God said to the people' is Origen's, to show what is not written.

title: For you
english: For if he had added: "Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: This month is for you the beginning of months," (Exodus 12:2–3) he would have been saying this without distinction both to Moses and Aaron and to the whole people. But it is said to Moses and Aaron: "This month is for you the beginning of months; it is first for you among the months of the year." And he is commanded to speak not this, but that on the tenth of the month they should take a sheep according to the houses of the fathers.

added_allusions.reason: The month-word is to Moses and Aaron; the taking is what is spoken to the people.

translator_notes: Witte insertion <οὐ>: Moses is told to speak not the 'beginning of months' word but the taking of the sheep.

title: For you
english: It is clear that that month was not then a beginning of months for all the people, but only for Moses and Aaron, to whom it was said. For a person must fully renounce the creation and this world, so as to grasp that one has almost been born another than what one was — in order to hear: This month is for you a beginning of months; it is first for you among the months of the year (Exodus 12:2) (Galatians 6:14).

added_allusions.reason: Heard only by the perfect: this month is for you a beginning.
Renouncing the world; possible.

translator_notes: σχεδόν kept as 'almost' — another Origen hedge.

title: For you
english: For that the perfect has a beginning of another birth and becomes another than what he was, the apostle teaches us. At one time he says: "The old man was crucified with Christ" (Romans 6:6); and again: "If we died with him, we shall also live with him." (2 Timothy 2:11) And of himself he says plainly: "I live no longer I, but Christ lives in me." (Galatians 2:20) (Romans 6:8)

added_allusions.reason: The old man crucified with Christ.
If we died with him, we shall also live with him.
Same died-with / live-with formula.
Quoted: I live no longer I; Christ lives in me.

translator_notes: γυμνῶς: 'plainly' (without covering), of Paul's speaking about himself.

title: For you
english: Such are those who, while still in the world, are able to hear that a first month and a beginning of months have come to be for them (Exodus 12:2).

added_allusions.reason: First month and beginning of months heard by the perfect.

translator_notes: Witte γεγον<έν>αι taken as 'have come to be'.

title: For you
english: That the perfect, having become another than what he was, then receives promises and blessing from God, let us consider. Abram does not receive the promises, but Abraham does. Jacob does not receive the blessings, but Israel does. And Simon does not become the first disciple of the Savior, but Peter does. James and John are sent as apostles when they have become Boanerges, that is, sons of thunder (Genesis 17:5) (Genesis 32:28) (Matthew 16:17–18) (Mark 3:17).

added_allusions.reason: Abram named Abraham when the promises are given.
Jacob named Israel.
Simon becomes Peter.
Quoted: Boanerges, sons of thunder.

translator_notes: Name-change as mark of another birth: Abram/Abraham, Jacob/Israel, Simon/Peter, James and John/Boanerges.

title: For you
english: And if we watch carefully everywhere, we shall find such things meant in Scripture: those who have been perfected have other names. They are no longer those people, but others than what they were.

title: Beginning and first
english: And so a beginning of months has come to be for them. And we should attend to [lacuna] the beginning and the first [lacuna], but "This month is a beginning of months for you; it is first among the months of the year." (Exodus 12:2)

added_allusions.reason: Lemma restated after the lacuna.

translator_notes: Witte p.96 lines 10–11 unrestored (L. ca. 6 Z.). Dots rendered [lacuna], not filled.

title: Beginning and first
english: For he could have said: "This month is for you the beginning of months and of the year," (Exodus 12:2) or: "This month is first of the year for you." But as if there were some distinction, he says that the month is both a beginning and first.

added_allusions.reason: Both ἀρχή and πρῶτος are used, not one word only.

translator_notes: διαστολή: a real distinction, not a flourish — the next paragraphs prove it.

title: Beginning and first
english: How then shall we find a path, and come to grasp whether "beginning" and "first" were said in the same sense, or were used of one thing and another — unless we are guided by the like things that lie in the Scriptures?
translator_notes: Witte insertion <ἑτέρου> kept as <another>.

title: Beginning and first
english: In the making of the world it is said at once at the opening: "In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth." (Genesis 1:1) For Scripture, knowing a distinction of "first" and "beginning," does not say: "He made first."

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth — not 'first'.

translator_notes: κοσμοποιία: 'making of the world', not 'cosmogony'.

title: Beginning and first
english: For the making of the world has had a beginning, the Creator, yet it was not made first by the Creator — for the Creator made many things before [...]. But the things that came to be had a beginning, whether first or second in word. For the first is properly said only when nothing precedes; but beginning is signified of things that begin, even if they come last. And whatever is first is also a beginning; but what is a beginning is not already also first.
translator_notes: Line 29 unrestored (L. ca. 2 Z.) left as [lacuna].
The rule is Origen's: every first is a beginning; not every beginning is first.

title: Beginning and first
english: And so that we may be led more fully to see what is being said, we shall take an example that will guide us to the thought. If some builder who has never built a house should come to building, we shall find in this house both the first and the beginning.

title: Beginning and first
english: For since he has never built, when he builds, then he builds for the first time. He has not built another house before this one. Yet even if this house he is building is first, it has, along with being first, a beginning as well — so that the beginning is taken of the foundation, while the first it has because he is building this for the first time.
translator_notes: Witte braces {ἔχει} omitted (doubled verb).

title: Beginning and first
english: But if he is already building this house as a second or third [...], the first the house does not have, but the one built before this, because of its being first as well.
translator_notes: Apparatus 18 L. ca. 3 Z. unrestored. Witte insertion <ταύτης ἀλλὰ τῆς πρὸ> kept as <but the one built before>.

title: Beginning and first
english: And so that we may understand more clearly, we shall take another thing. If several logs should lie near one another, we shall find the beginning in all of them — for each log, even to the last, has its own beginning — but only the one lying first has the first. And the first, being first according to position, has also its own beginning. Those that follow, having fallen out of the first, each have their own beginning.
translator_notes: ξύλα: logs/timbers lying in a row — a second example of first vs beginning.

title: Beginning and first
english: Since then a beginning does not in every case have the first, but the first in every case has the beginning, he says that this month is a beginning of months and first of the months of the year for them (Exodus 12:2).

added_allusions.reason: The month is both beginning and first.

title: Beginning and first
english: And so that what is said may not seem a mere assertion, we also call the Savior himself as witness, teaching us to have a distinction between beginning and first. For in the Apocalypse that is current of John he is saying: "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and last, the beginning and the end." (Revelation 22:13) [...] it is shown that the beginning is taken in one sense and the first in another (Revelation 1:8) (Revelation 21:6).

added_allusions.reason: Quoted (restored): Alpha and Omega, first and last, beginning and end.
Alpha and Omega.
Beginning and end.

translator_notes: 7–9 L. ca. 5 Z. unrestored between the quotation and the conclusion.

title: Beginning and first
english: And as it has been shown that of the first there must also be the beginning, he accordingly says here, because he is first, that he is also beginning: For I am, he says, the first and the last and the beginning and the end. For insofar as he is firstborn of all creation, he is first; and insofar as he is Wisdom, he is beginning. For so says Wisdom through Solomon, that "The Lord created me a beginning of his ways." (Revelation 22:13) (Colossians 1:15) (Proverbs 8:22)

added_allusions.reason: I am the first and the last and the beginning and the end.
Firstborn of all creation.
Quoted: The Lord created me a beginning of his ways.

translator_notes: ᾗ σοφία ἐστίν, ἀρχή: as Wisdom he is beginning (Prov 8:22), not 'first' in the Father's sense.
Closing quotation-bracket in the Greek is left open into 1.34; the English closes the Solomon sentence.

title: Beginning and first
english: And perhaps John too, knowing this, began in the gospel: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; this was in the beginning with God." (John 1:1–2)

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: In the beginning was the Word…

translator_notes: τάχα kept: perhaps John knew this distinction.

title: Beginning and first
english: For in the case of Wisdom he takes the beginning, and he says the Word is not beginning but "in the beginning." (John 1:1) For when the Son is with the Father in his own glory, he is not said to be first; for this belongs to the Father alone. For God alone is unbegotten, but the Son is not first [...] that [...] he wisely administers all things, he is beginning (John 17:5).

added_allusions.reason: The Word was in the beginning — not 'the Word was first'.
The Son with the Father in his own glory.

translator_notes: 27–29 L. ca. 8 Z. unrestored. Insertion <λέγει> kept as <he says>.
ἀ[γέννητος] rendered 'unbegotten'. First belongs to the unbegotten Father; the Son as Wisdom is beginning.

title: Beginning and first
english: Therefore also when he comes into his world John does not say: "the Word was first," (John 1:1) but "in the beginning was the Word."

added_allusions.reason: Not 'first was the Word' but 'in the beginning was the Word'.

title: Beginning and first
english: This distinction of the first and the beginning Jacob too, when he had become Israel, used when blessing Reuben: "Reuben, my firstborn and my strength and beginning of my children." (Genesis 49:3) For he knows both that he is firstborn and that he is beginning of his children.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: Reuben, my firstborn and my strength and beginning of my children.

translator_notes: Jacob-become-Israel still speaks both words, as Scripture does in Ex 12:2.

title: Beginning and first
english: And many such things in Scripture will be shown, which seem to those who read in passing to have sameness, but to those who meet them with care and attention are proved to have been distinguished.
translator_notes: ταυτότητα: sameness of sense, not 'identity' as a later technical term.

title: Beginning and first
english: For if he says: "Together the mindless and the fool shall perish" (Psalm 49:10) [...] together [...] they shall perish [...] the apostle when [...].

added_allusions.reason: LXX 48:11: ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἄνους καὶ ἄφρων ἀπολοῦνται.

translator_notes: 13–17 L. ca. 12 Z. unrestored. Not filled.

title: The Passover is not a type of the passion
english: Since then [lacuna]. The sheep is sacrificed by holy ones or Nazirites, but the Savior is sacrificed by the lawless and by sinners. And that the sheep of the Passover is sacrificed by holy ones, the apostle has also said: "For our Passover also has been sacrificed, Christ." (1 Corinthians 5:7) Christ is sacrificed according to the type of the Passover. He is sacrificed by the holy ones. And the Passover is a type of Christ — yet not of his passion (Numbers 6:14–17) (Acts 2:23).

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: our Passover has been sacrificed, Christ.
Nazirites offer animals; possible for [Να]ζιραίων.
The Savior given over by lawless men.

translator_notes: Opening unrestored. The load-bearing claim: πάσχα is type of Christ, not of the πάθος.
Holy ones sacrifice/eat; the lawless crucify — so the passion cannot be the Passover-type.

title: The Passover is not a type of the passion
english: For we must sacrifice the true sheep, if we have been made priests or offer equally with the priests, and we must roast and eat his flesh. And if this has not happened in the passion of the Savior, then his passion is not a type of the Passover. The Passover becomes a type of Christ himself, who is sacrificed by us (Exodus 12:8–9) (1 Peter 2:5).

added_allusions.reason: Roast and eat the flesh — the Passover act the passion did not perform.
A holy priesthood offering.

translator_notes: εἰ οὐ γέγενηται: if the roasting-and-eating did not take place at the passion — therefore the passion is not the Passover-type.

title: The Passover is not a type of the passion
english: For each of us first takes the sheep, then names it, then sacrifices it, and so having roasted it eats, and having eaten leaves nothing of it until morning, and then keeps the feast of unleavened bread, already having come out of Egypt (Exodus 12:3–11) (Exodus 12:14–20).

added_allusions.reason: Take, name, sacrifice, roast, eat, leave nothing till morning.
Then the unleavened feast, already out of Egypt.

translator_notes: Heavy Witte restoration of the ritual sequence; kept in brackets.

title: The Passover is not a type of the passion
english: And that the Passover is intelligible and not this sensible one, he himself says: "Unless you eat my flesh and drink my blood, you have no life in yourselves." (John 6:53) Must we then chew his flesh according to sense and drink his blood? But if he says this intelligibly, then the Passover too is intelligible and not sensible.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: unless you eat my flesh and drink my blood, you have no life in yourselves.

translator_notes: νοητόν / αἰσθητόν: intelligible / sensible — Origen's pair, not 'spiritual/physical' which flattens it.
τρώγειν: 'chew', the stronger Johannine verb, kept against a bland 'eat'.

title: The Passover is not a type of the passion
english: And let us see whether what has been said by the Savior follows what was said in the Passover. For as it was said there that the one who has not eaten the Passover shall be utterly destroyed from his people, so now he says of the true sheep that the one who has not eaten of his flesh does not have life. As there the destroyer cannot touch those who have eaten of the sheep, so now the one who has eaten of the true sheep flees the destroyer (Numbers 9:13) (John 6:53) (Exodus 12:23) (Exodus 12:15).

added_allusions.reason: The one who does not keep the Passover is cut off from the people.
Whoever eats leaven is cut off; related cut-off formula.
The one who has not eaten has no life.
The destroyer cannot touch those under the blood who have eaten.

translator_notes: κατα[φεύγει]: 'flees' the destroyer (Witte restoration).

title: The Passover is not a type of the passion
english: But if [lacuna] the Savior to have been crucified [lacuna] as we have said before, that the Passover is not a type of the passion but a type of Christ himself.
translator_notes: 20–22 L. ca. 8 Z. unrestored. Sentence continues into 1.46.

title: The Passover is not a type of the passion
english: For the Savior himself says: "As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of man be lifted up," (John 3:14) according to the type of the serpent hung on the wood by Moses, signifying nothing other than the passion of the Savior insofar as he was hung on wood. It is clear, then, that the passion will be taken according to the type of the serpent and not according to the type of the Passover (Numbers 21:8–9) (Deuteronomy 21:23).

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: as Moses lifted up the serpent, so the Son of man must be lifted up.
The bronze serpent on the wood.
Hung on wood; possible with Gal 3:13.

translator_notes: Witte insertion <τύπον> kept as <type>.

title: The Passover is not a type of the passion
english: For if he had said: "As Moses made the Passover in Egypt, so must Christ suffer," (John 3:14) it would have been undeniable that it had become a type of the Passover. Since he likened his passion to the serpent hung on wood, his passion would be a type of nothing else but this.

added_allusions.reason: He likened the passion to the serpent, not to the Passover.

translator_notes: Counterfactual: Jesus did not say 'as Moses made the Passover…'.

title: The Passover is not a type of the passion
english: And it would have been enough [...].
translator_notes: 7–10 L. ca. 14 Z. unrestored. Not filled.

title: The Passover is not a type of the passion
english: perhaps [lacuna] Christ is sacrificed, but he has not been crucified for all, but for those who are able to say: "But to me the world has been crucified, and I to the world," (Galatians 6:14) and for those who are able to say: "Having stripped the principalities and the authorities, he made a show of them, triumphing on the wood," (Colossians 2:15) and for those who are able to say: "But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world."

added_allusions.reason: Quoted twice: world crucified to me and I to the world; boast only in the cross.
Quoted: having stripped the principalities and authorities, he made a show, triumphing on the wood.

translator_notes: τάχα kept. Crucifixion 'not for all' but for those who can speak these verses — Origen's restriction, not smoothed.
Col 2:15 here 'on the wood' (ἐν τῷ ξύλῳ) as the papyrus has it.

title: Exodus 12:3
english: And now let us come also to the next wording: Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth of this month let each take a sheep according to the houses of the fathers, each a sheep according to a house (Exodus 12:3).

added_allusions.reason: Lemma.

translator_notes: Witte supplies the skipped clause in angle brackets from the LXX wording.

title: How the Hebrews keep the Passover
english: He does not say: "On the tenth of the month let them sacrifice a sheep," (Exodus 12:3) but "let them take a sheep." (Exodus 12:6) And this sheep they are commanded to sacrifice on the fourteenth.

added_allusions.reason: Take on the tenth — not sacrifice on the tenth.
Sacrifice on the fourteenth.

translator_notes: The whole argument of 1.51–1.55 hangs on λαμβάνειν vs θῦσαι.

title: How the Hebrews keep the Passover
english: So the Hebrews keep Passover: from the tenth they must take the sheep by houses and by families, and still feed them the eleventh and twelfth and thirteenth, and name them, saying: "This sheep is sacrificed for this one and that one" (Exodus 12:3–6) — their names not exceeding eighteen — and on the fourteenth it is sacrificed in the midst of the evenings. So from the taking of the sheep until the sacrificing there are five days. And this used to take place according to the sensible.

added_allusions.reason: Tenth to fourteenth; by houses; midst of the evenings.

translator_notes: ῑη = 18 names. A known limit on how many a lamb may cover; not invented.
After this Witte notes further lost lines (5–7 L. ca. 23 Z.) not filled here.

title: Take on the tenth
english: [...] that the true sheep is Christ, because he, being second after the Father, is taken through the second monad — I mean the number ten (Exodus 12:3) (John 1:29).

added_allusions.reason: The true sheep is Christ.
Taken on the tenth.

translator_notes: 5–7 L. ca. 23 Z. at the head of the page unrestored.
δεκάς as 'second monad': 10 = 1+2+3+4, or 10 as the second unit after 1; Origen's number-play, not filled out beyond what he says.

title: Keep it until the fourteenth

title: Loins girded
english: For especially through this desire he is able both to overturn and to wrestle down human beings — the loin being understood, as of the man, and the navel of the belly decently as of the woman — so that it may be shown that through such desire he most of all overpowers both the male and the female (Job 40:16).

added_allusions.reason: Loin and navel as the devil's hold, male and female.

translator_notes: {δὲ} omitted. Insertions <ἀνδρὸς καὶ τοῦ>, τῆ<ς> θηλεία<ς> taken as <man> / the woman.
εὐσχημόνως: 'decently' — Origen's own caution when naming the navel of the woman.

title: Loins girded
english: Since then Scripture bears witness that the loin is used of intercourse, we come onto a path of considering what it wants concerning the Passover: that we eat with loins girded according to families. We are commanded, when we chew the Passover, to become clean from bodily coming-together — the girding of the loin signifying this. It teaches us to bind round the seed-place and commands us to stop up the motions of mixing, when we partake of the flesh of Christ (Exodus 12:11) (Exodus 19:15).

added_allusions.reason: Loins girded while eating the Passover.
Do not come near a woman — possible frame for sexual abstinence at a holy meal.

translator_notes: Insertions <τί>, <καθαροὶ γενέσθαι> kept as <what> / <to become clean>.
συνουσίας / συνελεύσεως σωματικῆς / μίξεως: intercourse / bodily coming-together / mixing — not euphemized into 'impurity' only.

title: Loins girded
english: For if someone is athletic [...] competing and looking to those who are continent for the sake of a perishable contest, that they may receive a perishable contest, while he himself pursues an imperishable one to receive. For if someone should so gird the loin, he will also be able to leave none of the meats until morning (1 Corinthians 9:25) (Exodus 12:10).

added_allusions.reason: They are continent for a perishable crown; we for an imperishable.
Leave none of the meats until morning.

translator_notes: 18–20 L. ca. 4 Z. unrestored in the athletic opening.

title: Loins girded
english: Perhaps for this reason John the Baptist too, since he was perfect, had a leather belt around his loin — it being shown that he had put to death there all his seed-motion. The leather shows deadness: deadness had filled his whole nature (Matthew 3:4) (Mark 1:6) (Colossians 3:5).

added_allusions.reason: John's leather belt around the loin.
Leather belt around the loin.
Put to death the members — possible.

translator_notes: τάχα kept. Leather = νεκρότης, deadness, not merely 'austerity'.

title: Loins girded
english: And even the one who chews the Passover in marriage will gird his loin. For blessed are those who have wives as not having them, the apostle has said (1 Corinthians 7:29).

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: those who have wives as not having them.

translator_notes: {οἱ} omitted. Marriage is not barred; the loin is still girded.

title: Shoes on the feet
english: He also says that those who chew the Passover are to have the shoes on their feet — which might seem to some a contradiction of what was used toward Moses. For since Moses was treading on holy ground, he is commanded to loose the shoe from his feet. How then, when the Passover too is holy, are those who chew it commanded to have their shoes bound on (Exodus 12:11) (Exodus 3:5) (Acts 7:33) (Joshua 5:15)?

added_allusions.reason: Shoes on the feet.
Loose the shoe; holy ground.
Loose the sandal from your feet; the place is holy.
Loose the sandal; holy ground — possible parallel.

translator_notes: ἐναντίωμα: a seeming contradiction, which 1.110 will unbind.

title: Shoes on the feet
english: But these things are not at war. They are taken according to one thought and another. For when someone treads holy ground, he is commanded to have no deadness in himself, no longer about to cover any deadness of his. But when he chews the Passover, he is commanded to eat in haste for the sake of being ready, as the apostle also teaches, saying: "Having shod your feet in readiness of the gospel." (Exodus 3:5) (Exodus 12:11) (Ephesians 6:15)

added_allusions.reason: Holy ground: no covering of deadness (the hide shoe).
Eat in haste, shod.
Quoted: having shod your feet in readiness of the gospel.

translator_notes: νεκρότης: the leather shoe as a covering of deadness — same field as John's belt in 1.107.

title: Shoes on the feet
english: So that, when day has come, he may be able to go out unhindered, he is commanded to be shod. And in this it also shows something clearer about the resurrection of flesh, it too coming out with us as we go out of Egypt. For we must put to death the members that are on the earth — fornication, uncleanness, wantonness, idolatry, and the rest — and so come out of Egypt (Colossians 3:5) (1 Corinthians 15:42–44) (Romans 8:11).

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: put to death the members on the earth: fornication, uncleanness, passion, idolatry, and the rest.
Resurrection of flesh; possible.
The Spirit giving life to mortal bodies — possible.

translator_notes: Papyrus list: πορνείαν ἀκαθαρσίαν ἀσέλγειαν εἰδωλολατρίαν. ἀσέλγεια rendered 'wantonness'. Extra Col 3:5 members not in the papyrus are not supplied.

title: A staff in the hand
english: And so that we may see the likeness of the law to the gospel, we shall set beside the things said according to the law also things from the gospel. Moses, about to lead the people out of Egypt in order to bring them into the holy land, receiving commandments of God, is commanded not to have a shoe. And the apostles, being sent to lead the people from the nations out of intelligible Egypt, are commanded not to take a staff for the road, nor a bag, nor to have sandals bound on (Exodus 3:5) (Matthew 10:10) (Luke 9:3) (Luke 10:4) (Mark 6:8).

added_allusions.reason: Moses commanded not to have a shoe.
No bag, no sandals.
Take nothing except a staff — Origen's 'not to take a staff' follows the Matthew/Luke form.
Take no staff.
No bag, no sandals.

translator_notes: Insertions <νοητῆς>, α<ἴ>ρειν kept as <intelligible> / take.

title: A staff in the hand
english: As there those who eat the Passover in haste are commanded to have the shoes on their feet, likewise also in the gospel: those already able to sacrifice and eat the Passover, as has been shown, the apostle commands — as already having the loin girded in truth and putting on the breastplate of righteousness and having taken the helmet of salvation — already also to shoe themselves in readiness of the gospel, and already to have the staffs in their hands as already having shared in instruction. For the staff is a sign of instruction (Exodus 12:11) (Ephesians 6:14–17) (Proverbs 13:24).

added_allusions.reason: Shoes on the feet; staffs in the hands; in haste.
Loin girded in truth; breastplate of righteousness; readiness of the gospel; helmet of salvation.
The staff as instruction — completed in 1.114.

translator_notes: βακτηρία as σύμβολον παιδείας: a sign of instruction, not a magic rod.

title: A staff in the hand
english: For the one who spares his staff hates his own son, but the one who loves disciplines carefully — we have read in Proverbs (Proverbs 13:24).

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: he who spares the staff hates his son; he who loves disciplines carefully.

translator_notes: Book I subscription Ὠ(ριγένους) [πε]ρὶ πάσχα ᾱ is scribal, not rendered as Origen's prose.

title: A defense of spiritual interpretation
english: The sacred service and the sacred sacrifice were completed, in a mystery, in Moses' former time, as God commanded, for the salvation of the firstborn of the sons of Israel, because wrath was being brought upon Pharaoh and those under his rule who disobey the word of God (Exodus 12:12–13) (Exodus 11:4–7).

added_allusions.reason: Wrath on Egypt; firstborn of Israel saved.
The destroyer and the firstborn.

translator_notes: Book II marked β. Insertion πρὸς <σ>ωτηρίαν kept as <salvation>.
Sentence is one period through 2.3; the English keeps the hang but ends 2.1 at the Moses-clause.

title: A defense of spiritual interpretation
english: Now we ask whether it was completed only in their time, the deed having been fulfilled, so that it need not be received in another sense for the times that complete things among us, into which the ends of the ages have come (1 Corinthians 10:11).

added_allusions.reason: The ends of the ages have come.

translator_notes: ἐκδοχή: interpretation / taking of the sense. 'Another interpretation' is the spiritual reading he will defend.

title: A defense of spiritual interpretation
english: We have found the sacred and lawful scriptures not silent, but compelling us to the fulfillment of the commandments that were given, commandments now being completed in us, according to what was said: "Search the scriptures, in which you have life in them, and they bear witness about me." (John 5:39)

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: search the scriptures… they bear witness about me.

translator_notes: παρασιωπησά<ς>: not having kept silent — Witte's sigma.

title: A defense of spiritual interpretation
english: And the witness from them does not lie in a prophetic voice only. Knowledge has been written in the things that were done, which the great prophet arranges with knowledge for the race of the Hebrews, looking to the taking and the keeping, and further also the sacrificing and the eating by fire, and the posture of clothing, and the haste toward using up what has been sacredly offered, and the reducing to ash of what was left, and the lawful commandment being completed for their generations until the age as a memorial for them and for their sons. For he confesses that it holds not only of history but also of [lacuna] anagogy, as it is written: "Comparing spiritual things with spiritual." (Exodus 12:14) (1 Corinthians 2:13) (Exodus 12:24–27)

added_allusions.reason: A memorial for generations until the age.
A statute for you and your sons.
Quoted: comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

translator_notes: {ῳ} and {καὶ θυσίαν} omitted. {π ...} unrestored deletion left as [lacuna] before 'anagogy'.
ἐπιστημονικῶς: 'with knowledge', not modern laboratory science.
ἀναγωγή kept as 'anagogy' (the ascent of sense); a translator note names it.

title: To whom the spiritual interpretation is spoken
english: The spiritual sense, then, I try to set out by the grace of God, so that the salvation completed in Christ — God's effective salvation — may become clear to those who love to learn, as it is written: "As many as received him, he gave them authority to become children of God, who were born not of bloods nor of the will of flesh nor of the will of a man, but of God." (John 1:12–13)

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: as many as received him… born not of bloods… but of God.

translator_notes: || papyrus page 41. Insertion <σαρκὸς οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος> kept as <of flesh nor of the will>.

title: To whom the spiritual interpretation is spoken
english: For the adoption in Christ has become for us authority of so great a salvation — we who have come to be not of bloods and of the will of man and woman, whom he also confesses to be his brothers, saying: "I will declare your name to my brothers." (John 1:12–13) (Hebrews 2:12) (Psalm 22:22) (Romans 8:15) (Galatians 4:5)

added_allusions.reason: Not of bloods or of a man's will.
Adoption.
Adoption as sons.
Quoted: I will declare your name to my brothers.
The same saying (LXX 21:23).

translator_notes: Insertion <Χριστῷ> kept as <Christ>.

title: The taking and the keeping
english: For to these the salvation has come about through his blood, of Christ as of an unblemished lamb. For "as a sheep he was led to slaughter, and as a lamb before the one who shears it is voiceless, so he does not open his mouth. Who will recount his generation, because his life is taken from the earth, and from the lawlessness of his people he was led to his death. And I will give the poor in return for his death and the rich in return for his burial, because he did no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth." (Isaiah 53:7–9) (1 Peter 1:19) (Acts 8:32–33) (1 Peter 2:22)

added_allusions.reason: Unblemished lamb — possible with Ex 12:5.
Quoted at length from the LXX (sheep to slaughter; generation; poor and rich; no sin, no deceit).
The same Isaiah 53:7-8 in Acts.
He did no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth.

translator_notes: {τῆς} omitted. Isaiah follows the LXX including 'I will give the poor in return for his death'.

title: The taking and the keeping
english: For his death did not come from sin, but he himself bears our sins and is in pain for us, and by his bruise we all were healed (Isaiah 53:4) (Isaiah 53:5) (1 Peter 2:24).

added_allusions.reason: He bears our sins and is in pain for us.
By his bruise we were healed.
By his bruise you were healed.

translator_notes: οὐκ ἐξ ἁμαρτίας: his death did not arise from his sin.

title: The taking and the keeping
english: For as those were prefigured in a male sheep, so we in a human being who is as a lamb. As in a perfect one, so we in his fullness, he having completed the Father's will. As in a yearling, so at the end of ages — for as the year is a completing of months, so he too is a completing of law and prophets. As in an unblemished one, so in one without sin. As in the first month, so in the beginning of all creation, in which all things have been created. On the tenth, in the fullness of monarchy (Colossians 1:16) (Exodus 12:3–5) (John 1:29) (Colossians 1:19) (Colossians 2:9) (John 17:4) (Matthew 5:17) (1 Corinthians 10:11) (Galatians 4:4).

added_allusions.reason: As a lamb.
Fullness.
Fullness in him.
He completed the Father's will.
Completing law and prophets.
The ends of the ages.
The fullness of time.
In him all things have been created.
Male, perfect, yearling, unblemished, first month, tenth.

translator_notes: Insertions <ὡς>, <ἐν> kept. {τὸ ὡς} omitted.
ἐν πληρώματι μοναρχίας: 'in the fullness of monarchy' — the decade as completeness of the one rule; not paraphrased into 'the Father's monarchy' beyond the word.

title: The taking and the keeping
english: And until the fourteenth — of a second week — signifies a rest of two weeks, which from a first creation, that is an unseen one, has come upon a second, a visible one (Exodus 12:6) (Genesis 1:1) (Colossians 1:16).

added_allusions.reason: Kept until the fourteenth.
The first, unseen creation — possible Origen frame.
Visible and invisible.

translator_notes: Insertion <δ’ ἕ>ως; {ὃ} omitted.
Two weeks (14 days) as rest from first (unseen) creation to second (visible). Not expanded beyond the Greek.

title: The sacrifice and the eating as roast
english: And all the multitude of the sons of Israel shall slaughter him toward evening. And "all multitude" (Exodus 12:6) is of the sons of a human being who sees God — that is, of God's power. Toward evening: toward the ends of the ages (1 Corinthians 10:11) (Genesis 32:28).

added_allusions.reason: All the multitude of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening.
Israel: the one who sees God — Origen's standing etymology.
The ends of the ages.

translator_notes: υἱῶν ἀνθρώπου ὁρῶντος θεόν: Israel as 'a human being who sees God'. δύναμις θεοῦ glosses that seeing people as God's power.

title: The sacrifice and the eating as roast
english: And they shall anoint of his blood on the lintel and on both the doorposts. Lintel: the things above the head of all lambs. Doorposts: their bounds, through which they go in and go out in them — some enter in them, some go out from them — in which they are grasped as dwelling in them (Exodus 12:7).

added_allusions.reason: Blood on the lintel and both doorposts.

translator_notes: φλιά = lintel (over the head); σταθμοί = doorposts as bounds of going in and out.
The last clause is dense in the Greek and is not smoothed into a later church-door allegory Origen does not name.

title: The sacrifice and the eating as roast
english: And the sacrificing takes place in Egypt, under Pharaoh's rule — the rule that is according to earth and pressed by darkness, which is ignorance. And those under the rule of this ruler of Egypt are in much ignorance of blindness. He himself, having settled in, is held by the glory of his lifting-up, as he said: "Who is the Lord? I do not know, and I will not send Israel away," (Exodus 5:2) confessing the same as "I will set my throne above the clouds; I will go up into heaven; I will be equal to the Most High." (Isaiah 14:13–14) (2 Corinthians 4:4)

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: Who is the Lord? I do not know, and I will not send Israel away.
Quoted: I will set my throne above the clouds; I will go up into heaven; I will be equal to the Most High.
The god of this age blinding — possible.

translator_notes: Pharaoh's boast aligned with the Isaiah 14 boast; Origen names them as the same confession.

title: The sacrifice and the eating as roast
english: Those then who have listened to the prophet will complete this, being sojourners to him, having come to be under his tyranny in a time of famine, as having received from their fathers the most ancient oath-promise that their seed would be a sojourner — as toward father Abraham (Genesis 15:13) (Genesis 12:10) (Acts 7:6).

added_allusions.reason: Your seed shall be a sojourner.
Famine; sojourning in Egypt.
The seed would be a sojourner in a land not theirs.

translator_notes: πάροικοι αὐτῷ: sojourners to Pharaoh; παλαιοτάτην ὅρκωμοσίαν: the oath to Abraham.

title: The sacrifice and the eating as roast
english: For the sacrificing of this one, which was through them, was taking place in ignorance, because they did not know what they were doing — hence it is also forgiven them. For it is good that one human being die for the whole people. For it is not permitted that a prophet die outside Jerusalem — that is, of those who try to dwell in peace and righteousness (Luke 23:34) (John 11:50) (Luke 13:33) (Acts 3:17) (Hebrews 7:2).

added_allusions.reason: They do not know what they are doing; it is forgiven.
You acted in ignorance.
Quoted sense: it is good that one man die for the people.
It is not permitted that a prophet die outside Jerusalem.
Jerusalem: vision of peace — possible in the gloss 'peace and righteousness'.

translator_notes: Caiaphas and Luke 13:33 are used of the same death. Jerusalem glossed as those trying to dwell in peace and righteousness (Origen's etymology of the name).

title: The clothing of those at the meal
english: As they were under the law and, not having completed the very things according to the law, they fell from the salvation that is by nature through the law (Romans 9:31–32) (Romans 10:3).

added_allusions.reason: Israel pursuing the law did not attain it.
Not submitting to God's righteousness.

translator_notes: Witte: Textverderbnis, copyist omission marked <* * *> into 2.17. Sentence is broken; not repaired beyond the printed gap.
φύσεως σωτηρίας: salvation that is by nature through the law — kept, not recast as 'natural law'.

title: The clothing of those at the meal
english: [...] and that it has been completed in deed, they having received it lawfully, who in haste of faith and a tightening of bodily thoughts and a ready shoeing toward preparation of a good-working journey, staffs being handled in their hands, live in fear the life from this, which becomes salvation for them — and "unless you eat my flesh and drink my blood, you have no share with me." (Exodus 12:11) (John 6:53) (John 13:8)

added_allusions.reason: Haste, shoes, staffs.
Unless you eat my flesh and drink my blood.
You have no share with me — the papyrus joins this to John 6:53.

translator_notes: <* * *> as printed; insertion <διάγουσιν> kept as <live>.
The quotation blends John 6:53 with John 13:8 (μερίδα μετ’ ἐμοῦ). Translated as written; not silently replaced with 'life in yourselves'.

title: The clothing of those at the meal
english: These things the true sheep, the true lamb who takes away the sin of the world, the only one dying so that the whole nation of human beings may be saved — according to the high priest of that year, who was speaking without knowing (John 1:29) (John 11:49–51).

added_allusions.reason: The lamb who takes away the sin of the world.
Caiaphas, high priest that year, speaking without knowing.

translator_notes: ὃς οὐκ εἰδὼς ἔλεγεν: Caiaphas speaking not knowing — Origen's close.

title: The clothing of those at the meal
english: For the sacrifice is ready for the salvation of those sojourning according to the infancy of love of the nurse that has come to be for them, of the land that reared them — which nurse they had and used as a mother, not knowing the true mother, having been reared with a letting-go of flesh for bodies and with this world, sweeter for a time according to pleasure, held by ignorance of their paternal world — being called Hebrews (Galatians 4:26) (Galatians 4:1–3).

added_allusions.reason: The true mother, Jerusalem above — possible.
Infancy under guardians — possible.

translator_notes: ἀνέο<εσ>ιν as printed (ἄνεσις, letting-go). Dense period kept in short clauses as far as the Greek allows.
Hebrews named at the end: those sojourning, about to cross.

title: The clothing of those at the meal
english: For so he says: "The God of the Hebrews has called us." (Exodus 3:18) For as a crossing world is crossed over into the established paternal age, the turning of the children takes place, being effectively completed in the name of the Passover, which is called a going-over (Exodus 5:3) (Exodus 7:16).

added_allusions.reason: The God of the Hebrews has met with us / called us.
The God of the Hebrews.
The God of the Hebrews.

translator_notes: περατικοῦ / ἀντιπερατουμένου: a crossing world crossed over. Hebrews as crossers (πέραν).
ὑπέρβασις: 'going-over', distinct from Book I's διάβασις 'crossing'.

title: The clothing of those at the meal
english: For they go over through the name of this mystery, having partaken of it, having procured for themselves salvation: not to be destroyed together with the firstborn of the Egyptians from Pharaoh, who sits on his throne, even to the maidservant at the mill — that is, of those who are in a lifting-up of wealth and tyranny, in ignorance, and have not recognized the one who raises kings from a dunghill and seats them on royal thrones (Exodus 11:5) (Exodus 12:29) (1 Samuel 2:8) (Psalm 113:7–8).

added_allusions.reason: From Pharaoh on the throne to the maidservant at the mill.
The same range of the firstborn struck.
He raises the poor from the dunghill and seats them with princes.
LXX 112:7-8: from the dunghill to a throne.

translator_notes: The mill-maid and the dunghill-king are both kept; Origen's social contrast is the point.

title: The clothing of those at the meal
english: For he has given back [...] being held by ignorance to the bounds according to them — some by fate, some by chance, some by the rule of the ruler — because of the rearing toward him in a time of infancy, as they were reared, having forgotten the mother according to nature and the true Father who said: "Seeing I have seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their cry and I have come down to deliver them from the taskmasters and to deliver them from the slavery of Pharaoh and from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them into the land of the fathers, which I swore to Abraham and to Isaac and to Jacob to give them as an inheritance," (Exodus 3:7–8) (Exodus 3:17) (Exodus 6:6–8) (Genesis 15:18)

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: seeing I have seen the affliction… I have come down to deliver…
To the land sworn to the fathers.
Deliverance from Egypt; the sworn land.
The oath to Abraham.

translator_notes: Smaller copyist omission <* * *> after ἀποδέδωκεν γὰρ. Fate / chance / the ruler's rule kept as three pagan accounts of the bounds.
εἱμαρμένῃ / τύχῃ: fate / chance — Origen naming the rival explanations, not endorsing them.

title: The clothing of those at the meal
english: which he also did, having come at the completion of the ages for the putting away of sin through his flesh, having killed the enmity. Having come he preached good news to us who were far and to those near, having redeemed us from the authority of the darkness and having transferred us in his light (Hebrews 9:26) (Ephesians 2:14–17) (Colossians 1:13) (Colossians 1:21–22).

added_allusions.reason: At the completion of the ages, to put away sin.
He killed the enmity; preached peace to those far and near.
Redeemed from the authority of darkness; transferred into the kingdom of his light.
Reconciled in his flesh.

translator_notes: The long Exodus quotation of 2.22 is the antecedent of ὅπερ καὶ ἐποίησεν.

title: The clothing of those at the meal
english: For it is confessed that he transferred us from Egypt and from its rulers, whom he nailed to the cross, having made a show of them triumphing in openness over them in it. For this reason "Behold I have come — for it is written in the heading of a book about me —, O God, to do your will," (Colossians 2:14–15) having said beforehand: "Sacrifice and offering you did not want, but a body you prepared for me; burnt offering and offering for sin you did not take pleasure in," (Hebrews 10:5–7) (Psalm 40:6–8)

added_allusions.reason: Nailed to the cross; made a show; triumphing.
Quoted: sacrifice and offering you did not want; a body you prepared; behold I have come… to do your will.
LXX 39:7-9, the same words.

translator_notes: Insertion <ἐν παρρησίᾳ θριαμβεύσας> kept as <triumphing in openness>. Sentence continues in 2.25.

title: The clothing of those at the meal
english: through which offering of his a wandering world is being cleansed, coming to turning, and he makes peace of all things in the blood of his cross, the enmity having been killed, which is wrath for the destruction of those who disobey (Colossians 1:20) (Ephesians 2:16) (Hebrews 10:10) (Romans 1:18).

added_allusions.reason: Through this offering.
Making peace through the blood of his cross.
Killing the enmity in it.
Wrath upon disobedience — possible.

translator_notes: πλανώμενος κόσμος: a wandering world (not 'the world of error' as a title).

title: Using up the sacrificed meat
english: For if these rushed to obey the legislation according to what was said, having completed it in a bunch of hyssop — that is, in an exhalation of thoughts toward turning — which for them the true Passover has been completed, Christ who said: "I sanctify myself for these, and not for these only, but also for all who believe in you." (Exodus 12:22) (John 17:19–20) (Psalm 51:7)

added_allusions.reason: A bunch of hyssop.
Quoted: I sanctify myself for these, and not for these only, but also for those who believe.
Purge me with hyssop — possible.

translator_notes: Insertion <ὑπακούειν> kept as <to obey>.
ἀναθυμιάσει ἐννοιῶν: 'exhalation of thoughts' — hyssop as the rising of thoughts toward turning; not recast as 'incense of ideas'.
The period is awkward in the Greek (Witte's text); the English does not invent a smoother syntax than he has.

title: Using up the sacrificed meat
english: For they did not attempt the perfect itself in faith but in unbelief, not having known the scriptures, which the prophets were announcing. For "unless you believe you will not understand either." (Isaiah 7:9) "For I did not come to do my will but the will of the one who sent me," (John 6:38) and the will was that he be given for all who believe (John 5:30) (Matthew 22:29).

added_allusions.reason: LXX: unless you believe, you will not understand.
Quoted: I did not come to do my will but the will of the one who sent me.
Not my will but the will of the one who sent me.
You do not know the scriptures — possible.

translator_notes: οὐδ’ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε: the LXX Isaiah form, not recast as 'you will not be established'.

title: Using up the sacrificed meat
english: For if those too were making this haste, to bring him to the sacred service for their sanctification — which for them the commandment fulfilled: "You shall eat it in haste; it is a Passover to the Lord," (Exodus 12:11) which is a going-over of the Lord.

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: you shall eat it in haste; it is a Passover to the Lord.

translator_notes: The period is incomplete in force (if they had made this haste…); the apodosis is not supplied beyond the Greek.

title: Burning the remainder
english: For the one who has gone over the divine bounds — the bounds that were there through the disobedience in Adam — this one is Lord, who blunted the sting of death and took down its power, having given a leaping-over through good news to the spirits kept in Hades, and otherwise also having provided an upward road of travel into heaven through his own going up, doors and gates being lifted for his entrance: "Lift up gates, you rulers of yours, and be lifted, everlasting gates, and the king of glory will come in." (1 Corinthians 15:55–56) (1 Peter 3:19) (Psalm 24:7) (Romans 5:12–19) (Hebrews 2:14) (Ephesians 4:8–10)

added_allusions.reason: The disobedience in Adam.
The sting of death.
He took down the power of death.
He preached to the spirits in prison.
The ascent; leading captivity — possible.
LXX 23:7 quoted: lift up gates… the king of glory will come in.

translator_notes: ὑπερβάς τοὺς ὅρους τοὺς θείους διὰ τὴν ἐν Ἀδὰμ παρακοήν: he went over the divine bounds that stood through Adam's disobedience — Christ the Passover as overpasser, not Adam named as Lord.
ὑπερπήδησιν: a leaping-over (to the spirits in Hades).

title: Burning the remainder
english: And when it was heard a second time by the powers standing by, and they were examining who it is, they heard: "The Lord, mighty and powerful in war, the Lord of powers, this is the king of glory" (Psalm 24:8–10) — for king of the Father's glory, in which the Father is glorified, having reconciled a world to himself, not counting its trespasses against it, but having wiped out the handwriting against it, which was contrary, and he has taken it out of the midst (2 Corinthians 5:19) (Colossians 2:14) (John 13:31–32).

added_allusions.reason: LXX 23:8-10: the Lord mighty in war; the Lord of powers; king of glory.
Reconciling a world to himself, not counting trespasses.
Having wiped out the handwriting against us, contrary to us; taken it from the midst.
The Father glorified in the Son — possible.

translator_notes: The Psalm 24 dialogue of the gates, heard twice, with Colossians 2:14 as the content of the glory.

title: Burning the remainder
english: And these things were being completed in Christ, as he says: "For God was in Christ reconciling a world to himself," (2 Corinthians 5:19) and the reconciliation was taking place in the "as an innocent lamb being led to be sacrificed he did not know." (Jeremiah 11:19) For they reckoned a wicked reckoning against him, having known that "the Son of man must suffer many things and be killed and on the third day rise." (Mark 8:31) (Matthew 16:21) (Luke 9:22)

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: God was in Christ reconciling a world to himself.
LXX: as an innocent lamb led to be sacrificed, I did not know.
The Son of man must suffer many things and be killed and rise on the third day.
The same passion prediction.
The same.

translator_notes: Insertion <πονηρὸν> kept as <wicked>.
Jer 11:19 οὐκ ἔγνω kept as 'he did not know' (the lamb's 'I did not know' applied to Christ).
They 'having known' the passion-prediction while he 'did not know' as the lamb — the contrast is Origen's; not smoothed.

title: Burning the remainder
english: And of those who heard and were in a way grieved, he said: "It is to your advantage that I go away; for unless the grain of wheat dies, it remains alone, but if it dies, it bears much fruit," (John 16:7) which he confesses with: "Behold I and the children whom God has given me." (John 12:24) (Isaiah 8:18) (Hebrews 2:13)

added_allusions.reason: It is to your advantage that I go away.
Unless the grain of wheat dies, it remains alone; if it dies, it bears much fruit.
Behold I and the children God has given me.
The same quotation in Hebrews.

translator_notes: Origen joins John 16:7 and 12:24 in one saying; not split to 'correct' him.
Insertion <τῷ> kept as <with>.

title: Burning the remainder
english: Since then the children have shared in blood and flesh, he too likewise partook of the same, so that through death he might abolish the one who has the power of death — that is, the devil — and might set free these, as many as through fear of death were subject to slavery through all their living (Hebrews 2:14–15).

added_allusions.reason: Quoted: the children shared in blood and flesh… abolish the one who has the power of death, the devil… set free those subject to slavery through fear of death.

translator_notes: Extended Hebrews 2 quotation; wording follows the papyrus.

title: Burning the remainder
english: For the true sheep, which is Christ Jesus, of whom the sheep slaughtered in Egypt became a type, has set free from the slavery of the world-ruler of this darkness of this age, having delivered the Hebrews of that time from the authority of the then ruler of Egypt, which is called darkness, and Pharaoh "scatterer," (Ephesians 6:12) who scatters the works that are in the light of virtue through his ruling authority — that is, of a mind of those living in darkness (Colossians 1:13) (Exodus 12:21) (John 1:5).

added_allusions.reason: The world-rulers of this darkness.
From the authority of darkness.
The sheep slaughtered in Egypt as type.
The light in the darkness — possible.

translator_notes: Insertions <τὸ>, δ<ὲ δ>ιασκεδαστής kept: Pharaoh 'scatterer'.

κοσμοκράτορος τοῦ σκότος τούτου τοῦ αἰῶνος: world-ruler of this darkness of this age — the Greek is slightly broken (σκότος not σκότους); English follows the sense without rewriting the grammar into a cleaner genitive chain than Witte prints.

title: Burning the remainder
english: Let this be enough from me for now. I have sown fruitful seeds through these marks, so that what we have said in little, and incompletely, may be filled out at large by those who are willing and love to learn — as the Word has set it before us, so also to them, according to the same grace that is in Christ, may God grant it.
translator_notes: ἐγχαράξεων: marks / engravings (the written notes of the treatise).
Book I+II subscription Ὠριγένους περὶ πάσχα ᾱ β is scribal, not rendered as Origen's prose.
The closing prayer-wish is Origen's own incompleteness: he has sown starting-points, not finished the field.
